symptom: `call javascript action … (callback = Module.Flow, other = empty)` for Nanoflow-typed parameters was written as Microflows$BasicCodeActionParameterValue with the name as expression: check and exec passed, mx check CE0115/CE0117. describe left Nanoflows$NanoflowParameterValue mappings out, so editing a Studio Pro call spliced them away (8 mappings → 3).
file: sdk/microflows NanoflowParameterValue; mdl/backend/modelsdk microflow_read_actions.go / microflow_write.go (Nanoflows$NanoflowParameterValue), java_write.go codeActionParamTypeToGen (NanoflowType → JavaScriptActions$NanoflowJavaScriptActionParameterType); mdl/executor addCallJavaScriptActionAction, nanoflowParamArgRefusal, describe in cmd_microflows_format_action.go. Tests: *_2450_test.go in executor and modelsdk
cause: The JS-action call builder knew only entity-type vs basic parameters, the code-action value model had no nanoflow variant, and describe silently skipped values it could not print. Measuring it found a second gap: create javascript action stored a Nanoflow parameter as String, so no mxcli-authored action could even have one.
insight: **A describer that skips an unknown value turns every later edit into data loss.** The splice rebuilds an edited activity from the description, so whatever describe leaves out is deleted on the next change while 'Unchanged' on an untouched re-run hides it. Follow the existing precedent (Java MicroflowParameterValue, #1210/#1282) for name-not-expression and the empty form. Measured on 11.12.6: NanoflowParameterValue written, mx check 0 errors (was CE0117), describe → exec Unchanged, edited call keeps both nanoflow arguments.
